lehigh-2011-02.title: Volumes
lehigh-2011-02.body:
The bar has volume $2\cdot3\cdot4=24$. Each cube has volume $24/3=8$, so its side is $\sqrt[3]{8}=2$.

**Answer: 2**

lehigh-2011-03.title: Isosceles triangle
lehigh-2011-03.body:
Drop the altitude to the base of length 10; it splits the base into two 5s. Height $=\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12$. Area $=\frac12\cdot10\cdot12=60$.

**Answer: 60**

lehigh-2011-04.title: Two equations
lehigh-2011-04.body:
Let the first rectangle be $L\times W$. Then $L+W=14$ and $2(3L+2W)=72$, i.e. $3L+2W=36$. Subtract twice the first: $L=8$, so $W=6$. Area $=48$.

**Answer: 48**

lehigh-2011-05.title: Similar triangles
lehigh-2011-05.body:
Let the distance from the post be $x$. The person and the lamp form similar triangles: $\frac{5}{20}=\frac{8}{8+x}$, so $8+x=32$ and $x=24$.

**Answer: 24 feet**

lehigh-2011-06.title: Find the number of workers, then the profit
lehigh-2011-06.body:
Let there be $N$ workers and total profit $T$ dollars. Then $T=2.5N+25$. Paying \$3 each would leave three people with nothing, so exactly $N-3$ people could be paid: $T=3(N-3)$. Hence $2.5N+25=3N-9$, so $N=68$ and $T=195$ dollars.

At \$0.015 per cup, the number of cups is $195/0.015=13000$.

**Answer: 13000**

lehigh-2011-07.title: Right triangle
lehigh-2011-07.body:
Let $O$ be the center, $R$ the point where the chord meets the radius, $Q$ an end of the chord. Then $OR=15-3=12$, $OQ=15$, and $RQ=\sqrt{15^2-12^2}=9$. A radius perpendicular to a chord bisects it, so the chord is $2\cdot9=18$.

**Answer: 18**

lehigh-2011-08.title: Build up the coins
lehigh-2011-08.body:
Prices $1,2,3,4$ can only be paid with 1-cent coins, so four of them are needed, giving every amount $0$ to $4$. Adding a $5$ gives $0$ to $9$; a $10$ extends this to $19$; a second $10$ to $29$ (the most efficient way to bridge up to $25$); a $25$ to $54$; a $50$ to $104$. So the nine coins $1,1,1,1,5,10,10,25,50$ pay every price from $1$ to $100$.

A computer search over all collections of $8$ or fewer coins shows that none of them can pay every price from 1 to 100, so $9$ is the minimum.

**Answer: 9**

lehigh-2011-09.title: Factor and use signs
lehigh-2011-09.body:
$x^3+x^2-2x=x(x+2)(x-1)$. The roots are $-2,0,1$. The product is negative for $x<-2$, positive on $(-2,0)$, negative on $(0,1)$, positive for $x>1$. Including the roots, the solution set is $[-2,0]\cup[1,\infty)$.

**Answer: $[-2,0]\cup[1,\infty)$**

lehigh-2011-10.title: Angle chase
lehigh-2011-10.body:
The ray makes $50^\circ$ with $v$, and $v\perp h$, so it meets $h$ at a point $C$ making an angle of $90^\circ-50^\circ=40^\circ$ with $h$. After reflecting it hits $s$ at $D$; in triangle $BCD$ the angles at $C$ and $B$ are $40^\circ$ and $75^\circ$, so the ray makes $65^\circ$ with $s$ at $D$. After reflecting, it makes $65^\circ$ with $s$ on the other side and heads to $v$ at $E$.

In quadrilateral $ABDE$ the angles at $A$, $B$, $D$ are $90^\circ$, $75^\circ$, $180^\circ-65^\circ=115^\circ$. So the angle at $E$ is $360^\circ-280^\circ=80^\circ$.

**Answer: 80 degrees**

lehigh-2011-11.title: List the last two digits
lehigh-2011-11.body:
The last two digits of $2^n$ are: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 28, 56, 12, 24, 48, 96, 92, 84, 68, 36, 72, 44, 88, 76, 52, 04, 08, ... After 52 we get 04 again, which first appeared as $2^2$. So the cycle from $4$ to $4$ takes $20$ steps, and no shorter repeat occurs.

**Answer: 20**

lehigh-2011-11.title: Use the Chinese remainder theorem
lehigh-2011-11.body:
$2^n\equiv0\pmod 4$ for $n\ge2$, so we need $2^p\equiv1\pmod{25}$. The order of 2 mod 25 divides 20; $2^{10}=1024\equiv24\equiv-1$, so the order is 20. Hence $p=20$.

**Answer: 20**

lehigh-2011-13.title: Rationalize
lehigh-2011-13.body:
Multiply by the conjugate: $\sqrt{9000001}-\sqrt{9000000}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{9000001}+\sqrt{9000000}}\approx\frac1{6000}=0.000166\overline{6}$. To three significant figures this is $0.000167$.

**Answer: 0.000167**

lehigh-2011-14.title: Prime exponents
lehigh-2011-14.body:
$80=2^4\cdot5$. In $20!$ the exponent of 2 is $10+5+2+1=18$ and the exponent of 5 is $4$. We need $4n\le18$ and $n\le4$, so $n=4$.

**Answer: 4**

lehigh-2011-15.title: Convert and solve
lehigh-2011-15.body:
$2b^2+6b+5=81+9b+1$, so $2b^2-3b-77=0$, i.e. $(2b+11)(b-7)=0$. Hence $b=7$ (and the digit 6 is valid in base 7).

**Answer: 7**

lehigh-2011-16.title: Linear area
lehigh-2011-16.body:
The area is $\pi$ in 1930 and $4\pi$ in 1990, growing by $3\pi$ in 60 years, i.e. $\pi$ per 20 years. In 2010 it is $5\pi$, so the radius is $\sqrt5$ and the diameter $2\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt5$ feet**

lehigh-2011-17.title: Inscribed angles
lehigh-2011-17.body:
An angle inscribed in an arc is half the measure of the opposite arc (the one it does not contain). The four outside arcs together make up the whole circle. For each angle, the opposite arc is the circle minus its own arc, so each point of the circle lies in the opposite arcs of three of the four angles. The sum is $\frac12\cdot3\cdot360^\circ=540^\circ$.

**Answer: 540 degrees**

lehigh-2011-18.title: Count by digits
lehigh-2011-18.body:
Write the numbers $0000$ to $4999$ (leading zeros allowed; 0000 is excluded but has no 8, and 5000 has no 8, so they swap). The first digit is 0 to 4, none an 8: 5 choices out of 5. Each other digit avoids 8 with probability $0.9$. So the probability is $0.9^3=0.729$. (Direct count: $3645$ of $5000$ numbers have no 8.)

**Answer: 0.729**

lehigh-2011-19.title: Compose and solve
lehigh-2011-19.body:
$f(f(x))=\dfrac{\frac{x}{x+3}}{\frac{x}{x+3}+3}=\dfrac{x}{x+3(x+3)}=\dfrac{x}{4x+9}$. Setting this equal to $x$: $x=x(4x+9)$, so $x=0$ or $4x+9=1$, i.e. $x=-2$. Both are allowed.

**Answer: $0$ and $-2$**

lehigh-2011-20.title: Binomial theorem
lehigh-2011-20.body:
The term with $(2x^2)^4\left(-\frac1x\right)^2$ has degree $8-2=6$. Its coefficient is $\binom64\cdot2^4=15\cdot16=240$.

**Answer: 240**

lehigh-2011-21.title: Chinese remainder theorem
lehigh-2011-21.body:
$x^2-3x+2=(x-1)(x-2)$ and $91=7\cdot13$. Since 7 and 13 are prime, $x\equiv1$ or $2\pmod 7$ and $x\equiv1$ or $2\pmod{13}$. Each of the $2\cdot2=4$ combinations gives exactly one residue mod 91: $x=1,\ 2,\ 15,\ 79$. Check: $14\cdot13=182=2\cdot91$ and $78\cdot77=6006=66\cdot91$.

**Answer: 4**

lehigh-2011-22.title: Factor out $x^2-r^2$
lehigh-2011-22.body:
The cubic is $(x^2-r^2)(3x+c)=3x^3+cx^2-3r^2x-cr^2$. Matching: $3r^2=5$ and $cr^2=10$. So $r^2=\frac53$, $c=\frac{10}{5/3}=6$, and $\alpha=c=6$.

**Answer: 6**

lehigh-2011-22.title: Add the equations
lehigh-2011-22.body:
Plug $r$ and $-r$ into the cubic and add: $2\alpha r^2-20=0$, so $\alpha r^2=10$. Subtracting: $6r^3-10r=0$, so $r^2=\frac53$. Thus $\alpha=\frac{10}{5/3}=6$.

**Answer: 6**

lehigh-2011-23.title: Estimate each
lehigh-2011-23.body:
$\sin(.01)\approx0.01$, so $B\approx10^{-6}$ and $A\approx10^{-4}$. Both $C$ and $D$ are about $0.01$. Since $\sin x<x$ for $x>0$, $D=\sin(\sin(\sin .01))<\sin(\sin .01)=C$ (apply $\sin t<t$ with $t=\sin(\sin .01)$). So $B<A<D<C$.

**Answer: BADC**

lehigh-2011-24.title: Area decomposition
lehigh-2011-24.body:
Joining $P$ to the vertices splits the triangle into three triangles with base 1 and heights $h_1,h_2,h_3$. Their areas sum to the area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}$ of the triangle: $\frac12(h_1+h_2+h_3)=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}$. So $S(P)=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ for every $P$ (Viviani's theorem), and in particular this is the maximum.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$**

lehigh-2011-25.title: Prime factorization
lehigh-2011-25.body:
Both quotients being perfect powers forces $N=2^a3^b$. $N/3=2^a3^{b-1}$ is a perfect square: $a$ even, $b$ odd. $N/2=2^{a-1}3^b$ is a perfect cube: $a\equiv1\pmod3$, $b\equiv0\pmod3$. Smallest: $a=4$, $b=3$, so $N=16\cdot27=432$.

**Answer: 432**

lehigh-2011-26.title: Pascal's triangle
lehigh-2011-26.body:
At level $n$ the fraction of people in position $i$ (counted from the left, starting at 0) is $\binom ni/2^n$. The next-to-left position at level 99 is position $1$, holding $2^{100}\cdot\binom{99}{1}/2^{99}=2\cdot99=198$ people.

**Answer: 198**

lehigh-2011-27.title: Divide by rotations
lehigh-2011-27.body:
There are $6!=720$ ways to color the faces with the six colors, and the cube has $24$ rotations; with all colors different, no non-trivial rotation fixes a coloring, so each class has 24 colorings: $720/24=30$.

**Answer: 30**

lehigh-2011-27.title: Direct count
lehigh-2011-27.body:
Fix color 1 on top. Five choices for the color on the bottom. Of the remaining four colors, put the smallest on a side face; the opposite face has 3 choices. The last two colors go on the remaining opposite pair of faces in 2 ways, which give different (mirror image) cubes. Total $5\cdot3\cdot2=30$.

**Answer: 30**

lehigh-2011-28.title: Arrange the steps
lehigh-2011-28.body:
A path consists of 7 unit steps, 3 to the right and 4 up, in any order: $\binom73=35$.

**Answer: 35**

lehigh-2011-29.title: Tangent addition
lehigh-2011-29.body:
Let $B$ be the angle of elevation of the top of the building: $\tan B=\frac{40}{50}=\frac45$. The top of the pole is at angle $A+B$ with $\tan(A+B)=\frac{\frac15+\frac45}{1-\frac15\cdot\frac45}=\frac{25}{21}$. If the pole has height $x$, then $\frac{x+40}{50}=\frac{25}{21}$, so $x=\frac{1250}{21}-40=\frac{410}{21}=19\frac{11}{21}$.

**Answer: $\frac{410}{21}$ feet**

lehigh-2011-30.title: Use area and Pythagoras
lehigh-2011-30.body:
Let the legs be $a,b$ and hypotenuse $c$. Then $a+b+c=30$, $ab=5c$ (area two ways), $a^2+b^2=c^2$. Put $s=a+b=30-c$. Then $s^2=c^2+2ab=c^2+10c$, so $(30-c)^2=c^2+10c$, i.e. $900-60c=10c$, $c=\frac{90}{7}$.

**Answer: $\frac{90}{7}$**

lehigh-2011-31.title: Angle sum
lehigh-2011-31.body:
The interior angles sum to $(n-2)\cdot180^\circ$. If $n-1$ angles equal $150^\circ$ and the last is $a$, then $a=(n-2)180-(n-1)150=30(n-7)$. Convexity needs $0<a<180$, so $7<n<13$. The remaining angle is $30^\circ,60^\circ,90^\circ,120^\circ,150^\circ$ for $n=8,\dots,12$ (for $n=12$ all angles equal $150^\circ$). A convex polygon with these angles exists, since all angles are between $0^\circ$ and $180^\circ$ and their sum is right.

**Answer: $n=8,9,10,11,12$**

lehigh-2011-32.title: Two meetings
lehigh-2011-32.body:
After 1 hour the car and Bill are at mile 40 and Alan is at mile 4. Let the car drive back for $t$ hours until it meets Alan: $4(1+t)=40-40t$, so $t=\frac9{11}$. Then Bill has walked to mile $40+4\cdot\frac9{11}=\frac{476}{11}$ and the car is at Alan's position, mile $\frac{80}{11}$, so the gap is $36$ miles. The car now drives toward Bill at $40$ mph while Bill walks away at $4$ mph, so it catches him after $\frac{36}{40-4}=1$ hour, during which Bill walks 4 more miles. Bill's distance from the start is $\frac{476}{11}+4=\frac{520}{11}$.

**Answer: $\frac{520}{11}$ miles**

lehigh-2011-33.title: Factor
lehigh-2011-33.body:
$x^3-11x^2-107x+1177=x^2(x-11)-107(x-11)=(x-11)(x^2-107)$. A prime must be $\pm1$ times a prime, so either $|x-11|=1$ or $|x^2-107|=1$. Since $106$ and $108$ are not perfect squares, only $x=10$ or $x=12$ remain. $x=10$: $(-1)(-7)=7$. $x=12$: $(1)(37)=37$. Both are prime.

**Answer: $7$ and $37$**

lehigh-2011-34.title: Work backwards
lehigh-2011-34.body:
Let $x$ be the term just before 81. Going backwards the terms are $81-x$, $2x-81$, $162-3x$, $5x-243$, $405-8x$, $13x-648$, $1053-21x$, $34x-1701$. Positivity of the first seven gives $x<81$, $x>40$, $x<54$, $x>48$, $x<51$, $x>49$, $x<50.1$, which forces $x=50$; the eighth, $34x-1701=-1$, is then not positive. So at most $8$ terms can precede 81, and exactly one sequence achieves it: $3,2,5,7,12,19,31,50,81$.

**Answer: $(3,2)$**

lehigh-2011-36.title: Regular tetrahedron
lehigh-2011-36.body:
The centers form a regular tetrahedron of edge 2. Its circumradius is $\frac{\sqrt6}{4}\cdot2=\frac{\sqrt6}{2}$ (the center is $\frac34$ of the way up an altitude of length $\sqrt{8/3}$). The containing sphere is centered there and has radius $1+\frac{\sqrt6}{2}$.

**Answer: $1+\frac{\sqrt6}{2}$**

lehigh-2011-37.title: Lattice points under a line
lehigh-2011-37.body:
Since $\gcd(729,1000)=1$, the line $y=\frac{729}{1000}x$ has no lattice point strictly between $x=1$ and $x=999$. The sum counts lattice points with $1\le x\le999$, $1\le y\le$ line. The rectangle $[1,999]\times[1,728]$ contains $999\cdot728$ points, and by the symmetry about its center half lie below the line: $\frac{999\cdot728}{2}=363636$.

**Answer: 363636**

lehigh-2011-38.title: Coordinates
lehigh-2011-38.body:
$AC=\sqrt{2^2+4^2}=2\sqrt5$ and $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, so $\angle CBD=\angle DBA=45^\circ$ and $D$ is the midpoint of the arc $AC$ not containing $B$. Place $C=(0,0)$, $A=(2\sqrt5,0)$; then $B=\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt5},\frac{4}{\sqrt5}\right)$ and $D=(\sqrt5,-\sqrt5)$. So $BD^2=\left(\sqrt5-\frac2{\sqrt5}\right)^2+\left(\sqrt5+\frac4{\sqrt5}\right)^2=\frac95+\frac{81}5=18$, and $BD=3\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $3\sqrt2$**

lehigh-2011-39.title: Inclusion-exclusion
lehigh-2011-39.body:
Give each person one cookie first; 13 remain, and each person may get at most 5 more. Without the upper limit: $\binom{17}{4}=2380$. Subtract those where some person gets $\ge6$ more: $5\binom{11}{4}=1650$. Two people both $\ge6$ would need 12 and leave 1: add back $\binom52\binom{5}{4}=50$. Total $2380-1650+50=780$.

**Answer: 780**

lehigh-2011-40.title: Express in $p$
lehigh-2011-40.body:
$\alpha+\beta=2p$ and $\alpha\beta=p^2-2p-1$, so $(\alpha-\beta)^2=4p^2-4(p^2-2p-1)=8p+4$ (the roots are real for $p\ge-\frac12$). The expression is $\dfrac{8p+2}{2(4p^2+2)}=\dfrac{4p+1}{4p^2+2}=n$, an integer. Then $4np^2-4p+2n-1=0$.

$n=0$: $p=-\frac14$.

$n\ne0$: real $p$ needs discriminant $16-16n(2n-1)\ge0$, i.e. $-\frac12\le n\le1$, so $n=1$: $4p^2-4p+1=0$, $p=\frac12$.

**Answer: $p=-\frac14$ and $p=\frac12$**
